original_value: Recent advances in the availability of very high-resolution (VHR) satellite data together with efficient data acquisition and large area coverage have led to an upward trend in their applications for automatic 3-D building model reconstruction which require large-scale and frequent updates, such as disaster monitoring and urban management. Digital Surface Models (DSMs) generated from stereo satellite imagery suffer from mismatches, missing values, or blunders, resulting in rough building shape representations. To handle 3-D building model reconstruction using such low-quality DSMs, we propose a novel automatic multistage hybrid method using DSMs together with orthorectified panchromatic (PAN) and pansharpened data (PS) of multispectral (MS) satellite imagery. The algorithm consists of multiple steps including building boundary extraction and decomposition, image-based roof type classification, and initial roof parameter computation which are prior knowledge for the 3-D model fitting step. To fit 3-D models to the normalized DSM (nDSM) and to select the best one, a parameter optimization method based on exhaustive search is used sequentially in 2-D and 3-D. Finally, the neighboring building models in a building block are intersected to reconstruct the 3-D model of connecting roofs. All corresponding experiments are conducted on a dataset including four different areas of Munich city containing 208 buildings with different degrees of complexity. The results are evaluated both qualitatively and quantitatively. According to the results, the proposed approach can reliably reconstruct 3-D building models, even the complex ones with several inner yards and multiple orientations. Furthermore, the proposed approach provides a high level of automation by limiting the number of primitive roof types and by performing automatic parameter initialization.

result.paraphrase: Recent developments in the availability of very high-resolution (VHR) satellite data, along with efficient data acquisition and broad area coverage, have increased their use for automatic 3-D building model reconstruction in tasks that demand large-scale and frequent updates, such as disaster monitoring and urban management. However, Digital Surface Models (DSMs) derived from stereo satellite imagery often contain mismatches, missing values, or blunders, which leads to coarse building shape representations. To address 3-D building model reconstruction from such poor-quality DSMs, we introduce a new automatic multistage hybrid method that combines DSMs with orthorectified panchromatic (PAN) and pansharpened data (PS) from multispectral (MS) satellite imagery. The method includes several stages, such as building boundary extraction and decomposition, image-based roof type classification, and initial roof parameter computation, which serves as prior knowledge for the 3-D model fitting stage. To fit 3-D models to the normalized DSM (nDSM) and choose the best one, exhaustive-search-based parameter optimization is applied sequentially in 2-D and 3-D. Finally, adjacent building models within a building block are intersected to reconstruct the 3-D model of connecting roofs. The experiments are carried out on a dataset with four different areas of Munich comprising 208 buildings of varying complexity. Results are assessed both qualitatively and quantitatively. The findings show that the proposed approach can reliably reconstruct 3-D building models, including complex ones with multiple orientations and several inner yards. In addition, it achieves a high degree of automation by restricting the number of primitive roof types and automatically initializing parameters.
